title: Dagobert Renouf: Selling Comp AI to $30K/month, and why he left indie making for B2B
summary: Dagobert recounts sponsoring his wedding suit, then closing about $200K of annual recurring revenue a month in sales at Comp AI. He explains why honest selling works, why he now picks growing markets over artistic ideas, and why he thinks the indie-making culture is a poor way to build a business.

principles.text: Sell by being real: tell poor-fit prospects it isn't for you, and the ones who need it will trust you.
principles.quote: when you push someone away who actually needs it immediately, they trust you because they know you're not selling it to them.

principles.text: Start from a growing market, not from what would be a cool idea. Building as an artist held him back.
principles.quote: I was coming to it from the perspective of an artist and not an entrepreneur.

principles.text: Find an underserved market via search demand and competitor reviews, then build an alternative with a clear differentiator.
principles.quote: finding an undeserved market where people are searching for something going to G2 or Capira looking of like existing products what's working failing building an alternative with a unique differentiator

principles.text: Look outside social-media-friendly niches. Old industries lack competition and can pay far more than cheap SaaS.
principles.quote: that you can sell a SAS for like 100 times more than $9 a month, you know

principles.text: Solo building is fragile; co-founders let you rest and split the work, with one building and one selling.
principles.quote: when you're going at it alone, you cannot have a bad day, you know. You cannot rest basically.

principles.text: Aim for a higher income bar. Founder hours at about $5K/month aren't worth it once you've seen better.
principles.quote: I was going through the craziest like 70 hours a week with zero safety for making 5k a month. It's like way too low.
